features.description: Most-imported state primitives. useToggle/useCounter cover the majority of toggle/counter needs; history/cloned/cycle/stepper/previous/lastChanged round out local state.
features.evidence: Shipped 8/8 modules under src/lib/state/ (useToggle, useCounter, usePrevious, useLastChanged, useCloned, useCycleList, useStepper, useOffsetPagination), each with index.svelte.ts + index.ts, README.md, a jsdom suite and an SSR probe. 91 new state tests; suite is 266/266 across 42 files. Barrel exports all 8 plus their option/return interfaces. Zero assertions and zero suppressions despite no-unsafe-type-assertion: (1) useToggle avoids pushing a boolean literal into the generic slot by giving valuesToggle() the two values as arguments and calling it with an explicit T; arity-vs-explicit-undefined is carried in the type via rest args `[] | [T]` instead of arguments.length. (2) useCloned cannot structuredClone a reactive proxy (DOMException, pinned by a probe), so the default clone runs over $state.snapshot; the snapshot type is named with ReturnType<typeof defaultClone<T>> because Svelte does not export Snapshot, which keeps value exactly T for plain data with no cast. (3) useCycleList reads list items with a non-null assertion justified by the wraparound bounds check. Documented divergences: usePrevious returns T | undefined before the first change; useCycleList returns T (and -1 index) for an empty list, matching VueUse. Gates green.
features.name: State essentials

features.description: Pure reactive array transforms. All synchronous/pure — high test coverage without compiler; shared/ category.
features.name: Reactive array utils
features.evidence: Shipped 13/13 modules under src/lib/shared/ (useArrayMap, useArrayFilter, useArrayUnique, useArraySome, useArrayEvery, useArrayIncludes, useArrayJoin, useArrayReduce, useArrayFind, useArrayFindIndex, useArrayFindLast, useArrayDifference, useSorted), each with index.svelte.ts + index.ts, README.md, a jsdom suite and an SSR probe. 158 new tests across 26 files; suite is 424/424 across 68 files. Barrel resolves all 13 functions plus 22 option/return interfaces (verified with a throwaway type-level guard, since a symbol exported from two paths is dropped silently). Zero type assertions and zero suppressions in the whole batch: (1) overload dispatch uses the implementation signature's parameter UNION plus typeof narrowing, so useArrayIncludes/useArrayDifference/useSorted read a comparator function, a keyof T key, or an options bag without casting the unknown third argument; useArrayIncludes narrows with a declared isOptions type guard rather than isObject, whose Record<PropertyKey, unknown> predicate collapses the union into '{} | null'. (2) useArrayReduce keeps a single-generic implementation signature under two public overloads, so both native reduce paths are called with no cast - the accumulator type coincides with the element type only in the no-seed case, which types cannot express across the overload boundary. (3) useSorted's default comparator uses Number(a) - Number(b), which is the same ToNumber conversion the subtraction operator performs and keeps the function assignable to UseSortedCompareFn<T> without a cast. (4) useArrayFindLast and useArrayUnique delegate to native findLast and Set instead of hand-rolled reverse scans and O(n^2) loops. Documented divergences: useArrayUnique's default is Set semantics (SameValueZero) so 0 and -0 collapse, matching the reference's stated intent; useArrayIncludes defaults to SameValueZero (like native includes) and key comparisons use Object.is; useSorted's default comparator is numeric, so strings need compareFn; useSorted dirty mode is client-only and the SSR probe covers copy mode only. Gates green.
